conversation.content:
Good morning—my name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to help you settle into motherhood by checking on how you’ve been feeling lately. We’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS—which is a short, 10-question screen that looks at mood, anxiety, and self-harm thoughts in the first postpartum year. Everything you share is confidential and will be used only to guide the best care for you. We’ll keep the conversation natural, and it takes just a few minutes. Ready to begin?

Over the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I can laugh sometimes… but it feels like I have to remind myself to. It’s not the same easy, automatic thing it used to be. If my husband makes a joke I’ll chuckle, but it fades fast, and I don’t really feel it inside the way I did before the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes… yes, I can laugh, but it feels kind of forced. Like, I’ll smile at something silly my husband says or a goofy face the baby makes, but the joy doesn’t stick around. Most of the time I’m just too tired or preoccupied to find things genuinely funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like my mom coming over tomorrow or the baby’s bath time—but the excitement is kind of muted. Before I had her I’d be buzzing about little plans; now it’s more “that’ll be nice” than a real spark.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens almost every day. If she’s fussy and won’t nap, I immediately think it’s something I did—maybe I ate the wrong thing, or I’m not soothing her right. Even when my partner says it’s normal baby stuff, I still catch myself replaying it and feeling like I’m failing her somehow.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just be sitting there feeding her and my heart starts racing because I’m suddenly sure she’s breathing weird, even though she looks fine. I know it’s probably nothing, but the worry pops up out of nowhere a few times a day. I can calm myself pretty quickly, but it keeps coming back.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I haven’t had full-on panic, but there are moments—like when she’s asleep and the house is too quiet—when a wave of “what if something bad happens?” hits me. My chest gets tight for a minute or two, then it passes. It’s not every day, maybe two or three times in the past week.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some of the time I’ve felt like that. I’ll be trying to get her down for a nap and the laundry’s piled up and the dishes aren’t done, and I think, “How does anyone do all this?” It feels heavy, but I usually manage to push through.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’ve been tired and a little down, but once I finally fall asleep I stay asleep—unless she wakes me. The hard part is getting my brain to quiet down at bedtime; I sometimes lie there for 20–30 minutes thinking about the next day, but it’s not because I’m terribly unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I do feel sad some days. It’s not all day long, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon when I’m really tired—where I just feel kind of empty or like I want to cry. It’s happened maybe three or four times this week, and it lingers for an hour or so before I shake it off.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when she wouldn’t latch and once when I dropped a plate and it shattered. It wasn’t sobbing, just tears that came fast and then stopped after a few minutes. I didn’t feel hopeless, just overwhelmed and suddenly weepy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt tired and stressed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like myself again and be the mom my little girl needs.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2–3 weeks post-delivery  

**Patient-reported symptoms**  
- Blunted enjoyment; laughter feels forced, excitement “muted”  
- Daily self-blame/guilt over routine infant care  
- Recurrent, unprovoked worry about infant safety; occasional chest tightness, racing heart (no full panic)  
- Episodic sadness/emptiness, late-afternoon onset, 3–4×/week, with brief tearfulness  
- Sleep onset delay (~20–30 min) due to racing thoughts; no sustained nocturnal mood-related insomnia  
- Feels “heavy” or overwhelmed by household tasks; able to push through  
- Denies any self-harm ideation  

**Patterns / screening significance**  
- Persistent anhedonia + guilt + intermittent crying spells → concerning for possible minor-moderate depressive symptoms  
- Unprompted anxious arousal → possible comorbid postpartum anxiety  
- No safety concerns voiced; protective factor of strong infant focus  

**Risk factors noted**  
- Daily guilt/self-criticism  
- Recurrent unexplained anxiety episodes  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed  

**Screening summary (non-diagnostic)**  
Patient endorses several core mood and anxiety symptoms commonly seen in postpartum presentations. No self-harm risk identified at this time. Continue monitoring; consider formal depression/anxiety assessment (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) and appropriate follow-up care.
